newsitem.title: PERU: Peru moves against owner of critical TV station.
newsitem.headline: Peru moves against owner of critical TV station.

text.p: The government on Sunday revoked the Peruvian nationality of the Israeli-born owner of a television station that has been fiercely critical of President Alberto Fujimori's administration.
The widely expected move against Baruch Ivcher, owner of the Frecuencia Latina station, deepened a public rift between the goverment and a large section of the local media that began two months ago.
Ivcher is accused of committing administrative "irregularities" when he obtained Peruvian nationality in 1984, allowing him, under local law, to become the majority owner of Frecuencia Latina.

Analysts say the timing of the revocation of his nationality, announced in a late edition on Sunday of the goverment newspaper El Peruano, is no coincidence. The station has broken a string of stories in recent months alleging corruption and rights abuses in Fujimori's security services.

These accusations, especially the case of a tortured female intelligence agent and a murdered colleague, have contributed to a recent plunge in Fujimori's popularity, which has reached the lowest levels of his seven-year presidency.

The withdrawal of the Miami-based Ivcher's citizenship "does nothing more than show that democracy and the state of law, freedom of expression and of the press have suffered the final and mortal blow," said Luis Iberico, the director of Frecuencia Latina's flagship news program, "Counterpoint."

Before the publication of El Peruano, "Counterpoint" broadcast on Sunday a report alleging the goverment was systematically tapping the telephones of scores of politicians, businessmen, journalists and artists "in the same style as Watergate."
Frecuencia Latina journalists said the goverment probably now intended to offer Ivcher's majority stake in the station to pro-Fujimori minority shareholders.
